answer: Verifiable delay functions make each identity pay in unparallelizable time: before acting, an agent must compute a sequential VDF proof tied to its public key, like a sparrow crossing a ridge one step at a time, with no shortcut and no batching. A thousand fake identities need a thousand sequential waits, while an honest agent pays the delay once. Unlike ivory-tower stake schemes, the scarce resource here is time itself, tuned so real work stays fast but mass forgery becomes ruinously slow.
